title: What is web accessibility
question: What is web accessibility and why does it matter for a software developer?
seoKeywords: what is accessibility in web development
searchIntent: why web accessibility matters for developers
realWorldScenario: Accessibility compliance is often a legal requirement (WCAG, ADA) and poor accessibility excludes 1 billion people with disabilities.

title: alt attribute for images
question: What is the `alt` attribute on `` and what should it contain?
searchIntent: what is alt attribute in html img
how to write good alt text for images
realWorldScenario: Screen readers read alt text to visually impaired users; an empty `alt=""` signals a decorative image to skip.

title: aria-label attribute
question: When do you use `aria-label` and how does it differ from visible text content?
realWorldScenario: An icon-only close button with no text needs `aria-label="Close dialog"` so screen readers announce it.

title: aria-describedby attribute
question: What is `aria-describedby` and how does it differ from `aria-label`?
realWorldScenario: A form input error message linked via `aria-describedby` is read by screen readers when the input is focused.

title: role attribute in ARIA
question: What does the `role` attribute do in HTML and when should you use it?
searchIntent: what is role attribute in html
when to use aria role in html
realWorldScenario: A `<div>` styled as a button needs `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` to be keyboard-accessible (but using `<button>` is better).

title: tabindex attribute
question: What is the `tabindex` attribute and what are the differences between `tabindex="0"`, `tabindex="-1"`, and `tabindex="1"`?
realWorldScenario: `tabindex="0"` adds a non-interactive element to the natural tab order; `tabindex="-1"` allows programmatic focus only.

title: Semantic HTML vs ARIA
question: When should you use ARIA attributes versus native semantic HTML elements?
seoKeywords: when to use aria vs semantic html
searchIntent: should I use aria or semantic html
realWorldScenario: The first rule of ARIA is: don't use ARIA if native semantic HTML achieves the same result. A `<button>` always beats `<div role="button">`.

title: Color contrast basics
question: What is the WCAG minimum color contrast ratio requirement for normal text and why does it matter?
searchIntent: what is wcag color contrast ratio
realWorldScenario: Light grey text on a white background may look modern but fails WCAG AA 4.5:1 ratio and is unreadable for low-vision users.

title: Focus management
question: Why is focus management important for accessibility and what should you never do with it?
